summary: Intermittent p99 throughput collapse during midday caused by bursty internal health-checks exhausting dedicated slots
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated drops in throughput and elevated p99 latency for their reserved pool between ~11:30-12:15 UTC on weekdays. The effect is transient (10-40m) and correlates with sudden GPU slot exhaustion. Impact: Noteable Analytics observed ~70% drop in sustained throughput for their model routes and increased 5xx rate for batched routes. Business impact: realtime inference pipelines degrade; internal SLAs at risk. Environment: Dedicated capacity (reserved pool rsv-3492) in us-east-1. Observed across multiple models pinned in the pool.

Observations:
- Starts as a spike of many short-lived streaming sessions (0.5-2s) from a small set of tenant API keys.
- Slot allocation logs show rapid allocate/deallocate churn and ephemeral batch sizes of 1.
- Autoscaler reacts by reducing scale (interpreting churn as idle), then later ramps back, creating a sawtooth in capacity and causing p99 spikes.

Initial ask: Customer requested explanation and a short-term mitigation to avoid further SLA breaches.
steps_to_reproduce: Monitor dedicated pool rsv-3492 during a weekday midday window (11:00-13:00 UTC).
Replay small-stream traffic generator that opens 200-500 very short streams (0.5-2s) distributed across many keys at t=0.
Observe slot allocation churn in scheduler logs and p99 latency in console dashboard for affected routes.
Verify autoscaler decision logs for scale-down events immediately after the burst.
logs: scheduler.log lines (us-east-1, rsv-3492): 'slot_alloc: tenant=noteable-123 request_id=... slot=12 allocated; duration=0.8s; dealloc'.
autoscaler.log sample: 'policy=utilization_smoothing window=60s observed_util=0.12 -> scale_down target_replicas=2 -> execute'.
serving-runtime: 'batcher: created batch size=1 repeated 430 times in 300s; kv-cache hit rate stable'.
console trace: 'p99 err rate increase from 180ms -> 2.1s at 11:37 UTC; throughput drop 68%'.
investigation_notes: 11-Mar: Confirmed burst source is internal to customer (tenant keys). Customer later confirmed recently enabled an internal health-checker for their fleet that opens short streaming probes every minute across many endpoints.

11-Mar: Identified autoscaler smoothing misinterpreting high churn as low utilization because of short-lived connections; scaling policy uses 60s window and min_replicas=1 for this pool, allowing undersize after a scale-down.
11-Mar: Observed GPU slot fragmentation: ephemeral streams prevented effective batching, causing increased per-token overhead and reduced GPU throughput efficiency.
12-Mar: Correlated with sidecar heartbeats — sidecars that attach to user streams were triggering prefetches and then immediately releasing, magnifying slot churn.
Hypothesis: Short, high-concurrency probes from the customer's health-check flood the scheduler with allocation requests, causing slot exhaustion and triggering hysteresis in autoscaler decisions.
resolution: Mitigation applied (12-Mar): Added temporary tenant-level filter in serving-gateway to reject requests with health-check user-agent pattern 'NoteableHC/1.0' and return 204; this immediately stabilized the pool and restored baseline throughput.
Hotfix PR merged (infra#4821) to increase autoscaler min_replicas to 3 for this reserved pool and to lengthen utilization smoothing window from 60s -> 120s for pools with high short-stream variance.

Follow-up tasks created: implement explicit per-tenant short-stream quota and add metric 'short_stream_rate' to the console; runbook updated to include guidance on blocking synthetic probes in dedicated pools.
Customer action: Noteable Analytics will move internal health-checks to a low-priority route on a separate non-dedicated project and will throttle probe concurrency pending long-term configs.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged and escalated to SRE. Asked customer for timeframe and traffic samples.
Noteable Ops (customer) 2026-03-10: Provided pcap and list of internal health-check IPs. Confirmed they rolled out a new probe last week.

Diego Ramos (SRE) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally with traffic generator; confirmed autoscaler incorrectly dropping replicas after burst. Linked infra PR to adjust smoothing. (See github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821).
Ava Patel (Platform) 2026-03-12: Deployed tenant filter as hotfix and monitored for 45 minutes; p99 returned to baseline. Advising follow-up telemetry and stricter short-stream quotas.
next_steps: Finalize and deploy autoscaler config changes to all dedicated pools with similar usage patterns (scheduled 2026-03-15).
Ship per-tenant short-stream quota enforcement and a UI toggle for customers to mark synthetic traffic (Q2 work).
Work with customer to validate their probe redesign and confirm no residual failures for one week before closing ticket.
Create alert: 'short_stream_rate > 200/s for 5m' -> page SRE and notify support.
